item.title: Peyton Miller dazzles in playoff debut with New England Revolution
item.description: Peyton Miller dazzles in playoff debut with New England Revolution By José Nuñez Welcome to the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, Peyton Miller . The New England Revolution 's rising homegrown star stole the show during Saturday's Round One opener, causing an own goal and scoring a superb volley to secure a 2-0 Game 1 win over the Philadelphia Union at Gillette Stadium. “I think that just shows how much he has grown in maturity, if I can say it like that. It really shows that he is ready to compete,” head coach Marko Mitrović said of Miller's standout effort. “Yes, he is a really young player, but he is converting from potential to being a performer. That is what a performer does.” Big first impression Miller memorable playoff debut marked another milestone in a season full of them for the 19-year-old. Amid producing a career-best 7g/9a, the versatile wingback broke into the US men's national team in September and placed sixth in the 2026 22 Under 22 rankings. And in New England's first playoff appearance in three years, Miller led the Revs to their first postseason victory since 2020. “It’s surreal playing for my boyhood club, so I’m just thankful for everything and all glory to God. I thank the fans for all the support today," said Miller, who became the fifth-youngest goalscorer in playoff history. "My parents, my friends, are all here, so this is special.” On to Philadelphia Miller and the Revolution can close out Round One when the Best-of-3 Series moves to Philadelphia's Subaru Park for Game 2 on Nov. 28 (4:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). However, they're not taking anything for granted. That especially applies against an opponent that was dominant throughout the second half of the season behind the inspired play of teenage phenom Cavan Sullivan , Golden Boot presented by Audi contender Milan Iloski and others. “Philadelphia is a very demanding team, a team that keeps you on your toes for all 90 minutes," warned Mitrović. item.title: Bengals' DB fined for taunting penalty vs Steelers
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals defensive back Jordan Battle was fined $11,941 for unsportsmanlike conduct/ taunting during the second quarter of their NFL Week 10 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . NBC Sports analyst and former Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth was critical of Battle for the penalty. Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. "He just sat there and looked at him and cost his team 15 yards, and gave the Steelers a chance to wake up," Collinsworth said of Battle's penalty during the broadcast. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss in 2025. item.title: NBA officials miss Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds late in Bucks' loss
item.description: PHILADELPHIA - The Milwaukee Bucks haven't had a lot go right for them during the course of this season, especially in the midst of a current 13-game losing streak following a 132-129 loss to Philadelphia at the Xfinity Mobile Arena on Nov. 21. But they were on the receiving end of a brutal missed call that could have determined the outcome of the game in the final seconds. Trailing 130-129 with 4.8 seconds left, the 76ers were inbounding opposite of their bench following a timeout. All of the game referees were watching LeBron James inbound, and then positioned around the 76ers basket. Only James floated the inbound pass deep toward the opposite end to Joel Embiid, and as the big man collected the ball and tried to evade an intentional foul from Tyler Herro, he stepped out of bounds. Only no one was there to see it but the Bucks' bench, and the fans in that corner. No whistle was blown, and Herro eventually fouled Embiid with 1.5 seconds left. Though the Bucks did not have a challenge, that is not something that could be reviewed had Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins had one. "Well, Embiid, he did step out of bounds," Herro said. "But for ref, it is a tough play. 'Cause the ball was being taken out on the other side of the court. For him to see that you've got to have a ref on that baseline. So it was a tough call, a tough play to see as a ref. So, I get that one." Brayden Burries wasn't in that corner, but saw the video of the play later. "He was out of bounds, but you know, they're humans, they miss calls," Burries said. "It just so happened it was a crucial call. But, it's OK." While the officials did miss the call, it's what happened in the immediate moments afterward that inevitably hurt the Bucks even more. Herro was trailing Embiid trying to intentionally foul, but when he saw Embiid step out, he instinctively pulled up. As soon as he realized there was no whistle, he committed the foul with 1.5 seconds left. "It looked like Tyler thought, or the team, that he stepped out of bounds," Jaime Jaquez Jr. "I didn't even see what happened but obviously I believe him. I think he kind of like slowed down because he thought they were going to call it, but I don't think there were any refs on that side. Which is, weird. But, I don't know where they're supposed to be but that was an important view for them to take a look at. I don't know." Shortly thereafter, Herro's buzzer beating attempt to tie the game was ruled no good as the ball left his hand a split second too late. "I just had to get the shot off a little bit quicker," Herro said. "I thought I had a little bit more time. Coach drew up a great play for me. I had the shot I wanted, I made it, just gotta be able to get it off on time next time." item.title: Illinois falls to No.13 Iowa on Senior Night
item.description: Champaign, Ill. – The scoreboard might not reflect it, but this was a very tight game for roughly 3 ½ quarters. It didn’t end up going Illinois’ way, but the Illini gave No. 13 Iowa a run for their money. Illinois (6-5) fell to the visiting Hawkeyes 34-17, being shut out in the second half. After both teams traded field goals to open the game, it was the Hawkeyes (9-2) that found the end zone first. The score came via LJ Phillips, who set up his 2-yard rushing touchdown with his massive run just two plays before. Phillips, who finished the game with 150 rushing yards, shrugged off multiple Illini defenders on the 30-yard run. The Illini, however, answered with their own big play just minutes later. It was Brayden Trimble who found the end zone first for the Illini. Houser found Trimble on a short crossing route that would normally just pick up ten or so yards. But that wasn’t what Trimble did. He somehow tiptoed his way to a 75-yard touchdown. The scene was truly incredible at Gies Memorial Stadium. Every time you thought he was about to get tackled or step out of bounds, he just kept going. The ensuing review upheld that he did indeed stay in the field of play, much to the delight of the home crowd. The next two touchdowns would both come with some dramatic reviews right on the goal line. First, for Iowa, Addison Ostrenga took a pass to the right side of the Illinois end zone and extended to try to cross the plane. However, he lost control of the ball, and the play was ruled a touchback for the Illini, as the ball went out of the end zone. The play was then overturned after further review, and the Hawkeyes scored moments later. But the Illini had their own plans on their next drive. After Katin Houser led the orange and blue all the way down the field, tight end Davin Stoffel played the hero with just 13 seconds remaining in the first half. Stoffel caught the ball and was immediately picked up by three different Iowa defenders; however, the senior was able to lunge at the goal line, just barely crossing it to get his first touchdown as an Illini. That play would be the last time the Illini would score on Saturday. Both teams went to the locker room tied 17 -17, and one team didn’t leave that mark. It felt like every time Iowa needed just a few more yards in the second half, they’d always be able to muscle out the needed distance. On the contrary, the Illini couldn’t stop coming up short in the second half. It’s not the end you want on senior night, but Illinois will have two more chances this season. item.title: Ithaca football tops Menominee to reach Division 7 state final
item.description: The Ithaca football team is headed to Ford Field. Gibson Rondy and Greyson Merchant each scored multiple touchdowns to lead the Yellowjackets to a 34-26 victory over Menominee in a Division 7 state semifinal at Gaylord High School on Saturday, Nov. 21. The win helps Ithaca (12-1) advance to its first state championship game since 2017. The Yellowjackets will face Ottawa Lake Whiteford at Ford Field on Saturday, Nov. 28. Rondy had 21 carries for 180 yards and three touchdowns and threw for 60 yards, while Merchant added a touchdown run and returned a kickoff 94 yards for a score to lead the Yellowjackets. Ithaca trailed 20-14 at halftime but took the lead on a 57-yard touchdown run in the third quarter and then the Landon Bratschi extra point that followed. Merchant added a 10-yard TD run in the third. Menominee, the reigning Division 7 state champion, tightened the game on a 1-yard run by Jackson Myszak in the fourth quarter. But Rondy added a 5-yard touchdown run later in the quarter for Ithaca to answer the score. item.description: Enoch Hall is a junior running back/defensive back for Devine. (Courtesy/Devine football) Devine junior running back Enoch Hall has been a huge part of the Warhorses' resurgence this season. He proved it again last week in helping Devine accomplish something it hadn't done in over a decade - win a playoff game. It was the Warhorses' first playoff win since 2015. He's been the offensive engine for the Warhorses all season. This week, he beat out four fellow finalists in the poll to earn Athlete of the Week honors. item.title: Leistikow's 4 thoughts on Iowa's aggressive 34-17 win at Illinois
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Illinois — Some help in the college football world started to roll in for the playoff-contending Iowa Hawkeyes . As the Nov. 21 game against Illinois wore on before a sellout crowd of 60,670 at Memorial Stadium, the question became: Could they take advantage? The No. 15 Hawkeyes stayed bold, stayed aggressive and unlocked an impressive 34-17 win against Illinois to move to 9-2 overall, 6-2 in the Big Ten Conference. Now Nebraska, which upset No. 14 Ohio State earlier in the day, stands in the way of a 10-2 season and a possible College Football Playoff berth Nov. 27 at Kinnick Stadium. The defining moment of the game came on a fourth-and-goal call from Illinois’ 2½-yard line with 7 minutes, 28 seconds remaining. Iowa had started the drive at its own 9-yard line and marched the length of the field in a clock-churning possession that spanned the third and fourth quarters. Iowa expended all three timeouts on the drive, including on the play to set up this pivotal call. In a decision that rekindled the daring fourth-and-goal call in the final minutes vs. Oregon last season with Mark Gronowski, offensive coordinator Tim Lester dialed up a quarterback draw in an empty backfield. And Hank Brown, the pro-style passer, made an electric juke and high-stepped into the end zone to give Iowa a 27-17 lead with a 2-yard touchdown. item.title: Mets Showing Interest In All-Star First Baseman After Resurgent Season
item.description: First baseman Ty France The New York Mets let Pete Alonso walk last offseason and were unable to replace his offensive production. The Mets have some internal options, but none of them really inspire confidence in the team's ability to replace Alonso. In reality, there is no replacement for a first baseman of Alonso's caliber. However, there is one option in free agency that could be a huge upgrade for the Mets: Ty France. According to the New York Post's Jon Heyman , the Mets are showing interest in France. France was an All-Star in 2022, and he was solid in 2023. However, he had been unable to replicate his 2022 success until last season. From 2023-2025, France had a .686 OPS. He hit 20 home runs in 2022, but had just 32 home runs in the three seasons right after that. Last year, France hit 21 home runs for the San Diego Padres and slashed .295/.363/.502. He has won a Gold Glove Award in his career and is still an elite defender at first base. David Stearns has often emphasized his desire to improve the Mets' defense, and adding France would certainly help. The Padres are reportedly interested in bringing France back, and he is reportedly looking for a three-year deal. The Mets and France seem like a perfect fit, but with the Mets expected to spend big on Tarik Skubal, they may not be able to compete with some of the other offers France gets. item.title: 'Perfect so far today': Louis Riddick, Bob Wischusen put brutal announcer jinx on BYU kicker
item.description: Credit: ESPN Dread it, run from it, the announcer jinx arrives all the same. The BYU Cougars’ College Football Playoff hopes were on the line Saturday when kicker Matthias Dunn stepped onto the field with three seconds remaining to attempt a game-winning 37-yard field goal against the Kansas Jayhawks. If he made it, the Cougars would move to 9-2 and keep their national championship hopes alive. If he missed it, we head to overtime, where anything can happen. After the ESPN broadcast noted the length of the field goal attempt, game analyst Louis Riddick started saying, “What should be a routine,” but stopped himself, perhaps realizing what he was doing. The silence left behind was filled by play-by-play announcer Bob Wischusen, who completed the jinx. “Perfect from this distance during his career,” said Wischusen. “Perfect so far today, 3-for-3.” Obviously, you know what happened next. Louis Riddick: “What should be a routine…” Bob Wischusen: “Perfect from this distance during his career. item.description: [Getty Images] Kicker Charlie Smyth has been elevated to the New Orleans Saints' playing roster and has signed a new deal with the NFL franchise. The former gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in Northern Ireland, has started the last two NFL games for the Saints after being promoted from the practice squad. The 25-year-old was handed a second opportunity to be the Saints' kicker after Dan Carlson, who started the season as first choice, was released at the start of November due to mixed form. Smyth helped the Saints to an overtime win over the Cleveland Browns on his return to the team and then kicked a late 55-yard field goal in the 20-17 defeat by the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. NFL rules state a player from a practice squad cannot be used more than three times in a season, and Smyth has been rewarded for his impressive return. item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached a climax with the fixtures for the first finals weekend confirmed. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action – and South Africa have pipped New Zealand to top spot in their pool with a bonus point in defeat to Ireland. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned.
